idea.title: What agents keep telling us
idea.angle: The pain points we hear in conversations: slow replies, missed bookings, wasted ad spend
idea.hook: What agents in Ghana and Nigeria keep telling us

slides.heading: **Field notes:** what agents tell us
slides.body: Notes from our early conversations with agents in Ghana and Nigeria. No results to show yet. Just what we're hearing.

slides.heading: **Leads** aren't the problem
slides.body: Instagram DMs, WhatsApp, website enquiries: the leads are there. The complaint is always about what happens after the message lands.

slides.heading: A buyer asked for details. I got busy. By the time I replied, they'd gone quiet.
Slow replies cost more than **bad listings**
slides.body: A buyer asking about a flat in East Legon is often asking other agents too. The first helpful reply has the advantage.

slides.heading: **Viewings** die in the follow-up gap
slides.body: The buyer says "let me check my schedule." Nobody checks back. The viewing never gets booked, and nobody notices it was lost.

slides.heading: Ads don't fail. **Replies** do.
slides.body: You pay in cedis or naira to boost a listing. On a busy day the leads sit unanswered. The ad brought the lead. The process lost it.

slides.heading: **Building** for the gap, not the lead
slides.body: We're early: a two-person team, no client results yet. We're designing around these three leaks first: reply speed, booking follow-up and ad leads.

caption:
What agents keep telling us, in our early conversations.

Nobody says they need more leads.
They say the buyer went quiet before they could reply.
They say the viewing never got booked.
They say they paid for ads and the leads sat unanswered.

We're a two-person team, early, no client results to show yet. So we're sharing what we hear and what we're building around it.

slides.heading: It asks the **right questions**
slides.body: Budget, area, move-in date, renting or buying. By the time you check your phone, you know if this is a serious buyer.

idea.title: Busy isn't why you're losing deals
idea.angle: Manual processes can't keep up with growth; it's a system problem, not effort
idea.hook: Busy isn't why you're losing deals

slides.heading: **Busy** isn't why you're losing deals
slides.body: A note to myself after another week of talking to agents.

slides.heading: **Every agent** I meet is working hard
slides.body: Viewings in the morning, landlord calls at lunch, WhatsApp replies at night. Effort isn't the problem. I haven't met a lazy agent yet.

slides.heading: The leak starts when you **grow**
slides.body: Say you get ten enquiries a week. You reply to all of them. Triple that, and messages start slipping. Same agent, same effort.

slides.heading: I saw the message. I meant to reply. Then the day happened.
Effort can't fix a **system problem**
slides.body: More late nights just move the leak to a different hour. You need a process that keeps running when you can't.

slides.heading: Write down **where leads go**
slides.body: For one week, note every enquiry: where it came from, when you replied, what happened next. The gaps show up fast.

slides.heading: Start with the **first reply**
slides.body: Save a WhatsApp quick reply: "Thanks for asking about the Kumasi plot. I'm on a viewing, full details by 4pm. Buying or renting?"

caption:
Busy isn't why you're losing deals.

Every agent I talk to is working hard.
The problem shows up when enquiries grow faster than one person can answer.
More late nights don't fix that. A better process does.
Start small: track one week of enquiries and save a quick first reply on WhatsApp.

Where do most of your leads slip through: DMs, WhatsApp or ad enquiries?

idea.title: 3 messages to get landlords to list with you
idea.angle: Outreach messages that win more listings
idea.hook: 3 messages to get landlords to list with you

slides.heading: **3 messages** to get landlords to list with you
slides.body: Copy, paste, change the details. Shaped by what I've learned doing outreach for Kortexa.

slides.heading: Landlords don't want **another agent**
slides.body: They want fewer empty months and less stress. Every message below talks about their property, not your services.

slides.heading: Lead with **their property**
slides.body: "Good morning. I saw your 3-bedroom in Airport Residential is available. I get enquiries for that area. Can I share how I'd market it? Just 5 minutes."

slides.heading: Make yes **easy**
slides.body: "Hi again, no pressure. I can send a one-page plan for how I'd find a tenant for your Lekki flat. Should I send it here?"

slides.heading: Ask the landlords **you have**
slides.body: "Thank you for trusting me with your property. Do you know another landlord who's tired of chasing tenants? I'd give their place the same care."

slides.heading: **Specific** beats polished
slides.body: Naming the property and the area shows you did your homework. "I'm a real estate agent, do you have anything?" is easy to ignore.

slides.heading: **Reply fast.** A landlord who messages at 9pm shouldn't wait until tomorrow.

caption:
3 messages to get landlords to list with you.

Message 1: lead with their property, not your agency.
Message 2: follow up with something useful, like a one-page plan.
Message 3: ask the landlords you already work with for a referral.
Change the area and property type to match your market, from Airport Residential to Lekki.
And when they reply, answer fast. Interest cools quickly.
